prompt_text: Who is the best personal injury lawyer in Houston for a car wreck?
answer_verbatim:
I can’t reliably name one single “best” lawyer for everyone — the right attorney depends on your case details and what you need (trial experience, maximum settlement record, quick resolution, etc.). I can, though, help you find the best fit. Here’s how to identify a top Houston personal-injury lawyer for a car wreck and what to do next.

What to look for
- Relevant experience: substantial car-accident and personal-injury trial experience in Texas (not just general practice).  
- Track record: significant settlements/verdicts for wreck victims and client references or testimonials.  
- Board certification: Texas Board of Legal Specialization certification in Personal Injury Trial Law is a strong plus.  
- Resources: a firm with investigators, medical experts and the financial resources to take a case to trial if needed.  
- Communication: prompt answers, clear explanations and a dedicated contact person.  
- Fee structure: most work on contingency (no recovery, no fee). Typical contingency ranges from about 33% pre-suit to 33–40% if litigation proceeds; ask about costs and how they’re advanced.  
- Local knowledge: experience with Houston-area courts, judges and local insurance companies.

Where to search and verify reputations
- Texas State Bar Lawyer Referral Service and the Texas Bar website (for complaints/disciplines).  
- Houston Bar Association referral service.  
- Independent rating sites: Super Lawyers, Martindale-Hubbell, Avvo. (Use these as starting points; read reviews critically.)  
- Ask for referrals from friends/family or your treating doctors.

Questions to ask in a free consult
- How many car-accident cases like mine have you handled? How many have gone to trial?  
- What results have you gotten (settlements/verdicts) for similar cases?  
- Who will handle my case day-to-day? Will you personally?  
- What is your fee and how are costs handled?  
- How do you communicate updates and how often?  
- What is the likely timeline and strategy for my case?

Immediate practical steps if you haven’t already taken them
- Get medical care and keep records (treatment notes, bills).  
- Preserve evidence: photos of injuries/vehicles/scene, witness info, police report number.  
- Do not give recorded statements to the other driver’s insurer without a lawyer.  
- Contact 2–3 attorneys for free consultations and compare answers.

If you want, I can:
- Pull together a short list of highly rated Houston personal-injury attorneys and firms (with contact info and why they might fit) — tell me your ZIP code/neighborhood and any case details (severity of injuries, disputed fault, insurance limits, deadlines).
